αἰδοίοισιν: αἰδοῖος — held in respect, revered; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
αἵδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., fem. nom. pl., agreeing with βόες: ’these (cattle)’
αὐτούς: αὐτός — self; masc. acc. pl.: ’them’ · also intensive, ’the very men themselves’ (with a following τε … τε) · also ’ourselves’, first person, coordinate with another object (νῆάς τε καὶ αὐτούς ’both the ships and ourselves’)
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)

αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
αὖτις: αὖτις — back, again, once more; adv. (= αὖθις)
βελέεσσιν: βέλος — shot, arrow, dart; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι(ν)
βιότοιο: βίοτος — life, livelihood; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
βροτοῖσιν: βροτός — mortal, mortal man; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic -οῖς)
γένηται: γίγνομαι — come to be, happen; aor. subj. 3 sg., in a temporal clause with ἄν/κε: ’shall come’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a direct question of doubt/deliberation, no ἄν/κε: τί … γένηται; ’what is to happen?’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg., prospective in a negative statement with a relative clause: οὐδὲ γένηται ’nor ever shall there be’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a general relative clause without ἄν/κε: ’whatever shall come to pass’ (ὅσσα γένηται) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a fear clause after μή: ’lest it become’ (μή … ἕλωρ … γένηται ’lest it become prey’) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in an indirect clause after ὅπως: ’(consider) how it may turn out’ (ὅπως ὄχ’ ἄριστα γένηται)
γέροντι: γέρων — old man; masc. dat. sg.
γήραϊ: γῆρας — old age; neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic γήρᾳ)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γυναιξί: γυνή — woman, wife; fem. dat. pl.
δίχα: δίχα — apart, in two, asunder; adv. (δίχα ... ἥνδανε βουλή, lit. ’counsel pleased split in two’, i.e. was divided)
δαΐφρονος: δαΐφρων — wise-minded, or perhaps ’warlike’; sense disputed (from δαῆναι ’learn’ or δάϊς ’battle’); masc. gen. sg.
δειλοῖσι: δειλός — wretched, miserable; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οῖς)
δειπνήσας: δειπνέω — dine, take a meal; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having dined’
δεσμῷ: δεσμός — bond, fetter; masc. dat. sg.
δεσποίνης: δέσποινα — mistress, lady; fem. gen. sg.
δεῦρ: δεῦρο — hither, here; adv., elided (δεῦρ’ = δεῦρο)
διὶ: Ζεύς — Zeus, chief of the gods; masc. dat. sg.
δμώεσσιν: δμώς — servant, slave (male); masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσιν (= Attic δμωσί)
δμῶες: δμώς — servant, slave (male); masc. nom. pl.
δοίην: δίδωμι — give; aor. opt. 1 sg.: ’I would give’
δυσμενέες: δυσμενής — hostile, ill-disposed; used substantivally, ’enemies’; masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic δυσμενεῖς)
δύω: δύο — two; numeral, epic by-form δύω, indeclinable
δώμαθ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώμαθ’ = δώματα before a rough breathing)
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῆμον: δῆμος — people, land, community; masc. acc. sg.
δῶ: δῶ — house, home; indeclinable epic noun (= δῶμα), used as nom./acc. sg. · also δίδωμι ’give’: aor. subj. 1 sg., ’I may give’ (ἵνα τοι δῶ ’that I may give you’)
δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb: ’the house’
εἰπὲ: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. imper. 2 sg.
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’) · also with opt., of an aim in view: ’in case, to see if’ (εἴ τινά … λάβοι ’in case he might catch someone’) · also in ὡς εἴ τ’ + opt., ’as if’ · also in ὡς εἴ τε with no verb or optative expressed: ’as if’
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; impersonal + inf.: ’it might be possible for him’ · also in a wish with a dat. of the person: ’may there be (for us)’ (εἴη μὲν νῦν νῶϊν … ἐδωδὴ ’may there be food for us two’)
εἴμ: εἰμί — be; pres. 1 sg., elided (εἴμ’ = εἰμί): ’I am’
εἵματ: εἷμα — garment, clothing; neut. acc. pl., elided (εἵματ’ = εἵματα)
εὔμαιε: Εὔμαιος — Eumaeus, the swineherd; masc. voc. sg.
εὔμηλος: Εὔμηλος — Eumelus, a man of Pherae, husband of Iphthime; masc. nom. sg.
εὔχεται: εὔχομαι — claim, boast, profess; pres. 3 sg.: ’claims (to be)’
εὔχομαι: εὔχομαι — declare oneself, avow, boast, pray; pres. 1 sg.: ’I declare myself (to be)’
εὕδειν: εὕδω — sleep; pres. inf.: ’to sleep’ (with ὤρνυντο, ’bestirred themselves to sleep’)
ζώει: ζώω (Attic ζάω) — live, be alive; pres. 3 sg.
θανάτῳ: θάνατος — death; masc. dat. sg., dat. of means: ’by a (pitiful) death’ · also dat. after ἐοικώς ’like’: ’like death’ (θανάτῳ ἄγχιστα ἐοικώς ’most like death’)
θεοὶ: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θηλυτέρῃσι: θηλύτερος — female, of womankind (epic comparative form of θῆλυς); fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι (= Attic -αις)
θυγατέρ: θυγάτηρ — daughter; dat. sg. θυγατέρι with ι elided (or acc. θυγατέρα with α elided)
θυμὸν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg. · also the life that leaves the body: ’life’ (μελιηδέα θυμὸν ἀπηύρα ’took away (my) honey-sweet life’)
θυμὸς: θυμός — heart, spirit, desire; nom. sg.
θύραζε: θύραζε — to the outside, out of doors; adv., directional suffix -δε (= -ζε after a vowel)
θῆκεν: τίθημι — put, place; aor. 3 sg. · also ’make (someone a certain way)’, with double acc.: ’made him (taller)’
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὃς δέ κ’ … ἵκηται ’whoever comes’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κ’ ἐλθὼν … εἴποιμι ’and I would go and tell’)
κάτα: κατά — down, throughout; prep. + acc., placed after its noun with anastrophe: κραναὴν Ἰθάκην κάτα ’throughout rocky Ithaca’ · also standing after its verb, not after a noun: ἔχῃ κάτα δῆμον ἅπαντα ’holds throughout the whole land’ (κατά + acc., or tmesis for κατέχῃ)
καθύπερθεν: καθύπερθεν — from above, on top; adv.
κακὸν: κακός — bad, evil; masc./neut. acc. sg.: ’by an evil (fate)’, inner acc. with μόρον · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (τι … κακὸν … μελέτω ’let no evil thing be a care’) · also neut. acc. sg. as a plain substantive, direct object: ’harm, evil’ (κακὸν ἀλλοδαποῖσι φέροντες ’bringing harm to men of other lands’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ἦμαρ: ’evil’ (κακὸν ἦμαρ ’the evil day’) · also masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’base, cowardly’ (κακὸν καὶ ἀνήνορα ’base and unmanned’) · also neut. acc. sg. attributive with πῆμα: ’evil’ (πῆμα κακὸν ’evil harm’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: κακὸν … βάζειν ’(it is) bad to speak’ · also neut. acc. sg. governed by ἐς: ’into evil’ (ἐς κακὸν … βάλῃσθα) · also neut. acc. sg. subject of an infinitive: ’an evil’ (κακὸν ἔμμεναι ’that an evil is’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of εἴη: ’evil’ (μή τι κακὸν … εἴη ’and may no evil be’) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive with ῥάκος: ’vile’ (ῥάκος ἄλλο κακὸν ’another, a vile rag’)
καλέονται: καλέω — call, name; pres. 3 pl. pass., epic uncontracted (= Attic καλοῦνται)
καλή: καλός — fine, fair; fem. nom. sg.
καλὰ: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; neut. acc. pl.
κατ: κατά (elided κατ’) — down from, throughout; + gen./acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (κατ’ … ἕζετο = κατέζετο ’sat down’)
κατάλεξον: καταλέγω — recount in full and in order (not yet ’choose’, as later); aor. imper. 2 sg.
κατέπεφνεν: πέφνω (defective, found only in the aorist) — slay, kill; redupl. aor. 3 sg. of the compound κατα-πέφνω: ’slew’
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … ἐποτρύνῃ ’until … urges on’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κε πίῃ) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever, as soon as’ (ὅτε … κε θάνῃσιν; ἐπεί κε … λίπῃ) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κε … ἀκούσῃς) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κε λίσσηαι ’but if you beg’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καὶ νύ κε … βάλεν ’and she would have hurled’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κε θάνωμεν ’either we may die’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κε … μαχοίμην ’I would fight’)
κείνη: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); fem. nom. sg.
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’ · also + aor. indic. of a future event pictured as already accomplished, an eventual near-certainty rather than a counterfactual: ἤ κεν ... κτεῖνεν ’or he may well have killed (him) already’ · also + subj. in a relative clause, prospective: ’who is to, who will’ (ἥ κεν ἄγῃσι ’(a wagon) that shall carry’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κεν … δαινύῃ ’whenever you feast’) · also + subj. in the protasis of a condition after αἴ: ’if ever’ · also + opt., potential: ’might, may’ · also + opt. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κεν … ἀφικοίμεθα ’but if we should reach’) · also + fut. indic. or short-vowel subj. in an apodosis: ’will’ (αἶψά κεν … τεύξομεν ’at once we will build’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἴ κεν … ἵκωμαι ’if I should come’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κεν ἁλώῃ ’or he may be caught’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κεν ὀπυίῃ ’whoever marries’)
κερδαλέον: κερδαλέος — crafty, cunning (from κέρδος ’gain’); masc. acc. sg.
κηρόθι: κῆρ — heart; with the suffix -θι of place: ’in the heart’, adv.
κλισίῃ: κλισίη — hut, shelter; fem. dat. sg., Ionic η
κοίλῃ: κοῖλος — hollow; fem. dat. sg., standing epithet of ships
κούρη: κούρη — girl, daughter; fem. nom. sg.
κρήνῃ: κρήνη — spring, fountain; fem. dat. sg.
κυδαλίμοιο: κυδάλιμος — glorious, famous; adj., masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
λίην: λίαν — very much, exceedingly; adv., Ionic λίην (= Attic λίαν)
λαέρτης: Λαέρτης — Laertes, father of Odysseus; masc. nom. sg.
λευγαλέῳ: λευγαλέος — pitiful, sorry, miserable; masc. dat. sg.
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
μάκαρες: μάκαρ — blessed, happy (esp. of the gods); masc. nom. pl. · also voc. pl. in address: μάκαρες θεοί ’blessed gods!’
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλιστα: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα: ’most of all, especially’
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’) · also μένω — stay, wait; pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (μέν’ = μένε): ’stay’
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’ · also μή + fut. inf. after a verb of swearing/promising, negating its content: μή ... βουλευσέμεν ’that ... will not plan’ · also ’lest’ with the subj. after a primary verb (μή πώς ... χαλεπήνῃ ’lest he be harsh’) · also in a question expecting the answer ’no’, after ἦ: ἦ μή … φάσθ’ ἔμμεναι; ’surely you do not say … are?’ · also ’lest’ + subj. after a past verb of urging (κελόμην … μή … λάθηται ’I urged … lest he forget’) · also in a condition, ’if … not’ (εἰ … μή τίς σε βιάζεται) · also with an infinitive used as an imperative, a prohibition: μή μ’ … καταλείπειν ’do not leave me’ · also negating a purpose clause after ἵνα: ’so that … not’ (ἵνα μή τι … ἀλγήσετε ’so that you may not suffer’) · also with the optative, a negative wish: ’may … not’ (μή … ἀντιβολήσαις)
μίγη: μίγνυμι — mix, unite; aor. pass. (sense mid.) 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐμίγη): ’was united (with), lay (with)’ + dat.
μεγάλη: μέγας — great, large; fem. nom. sg.
μεγάροις: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. pl.: ‘in the halls’
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μελέων: μέλος — limb; neut. gen. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic μελῶν): ’of the limbs’
μελαίνῃ: μέλας — black; standing epithet of ships; fem. dat. sg. μέλαινα · also modifying a different noun, not a ship (μελαίνῃ φρικί ’with a dark ripple’, of the sea’s surface)
μετέειπε: μετεῖπον — speak among, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic μετεῖπε)
μεταλλᾷς: μεταλλάω — inquire after, ask about; pres. 2 sg.
μεταλλῆσαι: μεταλλάω — inquire, ask about; aor. inf.
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · with acc. also ’in quest of, in search of’ (μετὰ χαλκόν ’after bronze’) · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also adverb, ’among them, in their midst’: μετὰ δὲ πρέπει ἀγρομένοισιν ’and he stands out among the gathered’ · also as preverb in tmesis (μετὰ … βεβήκει = μεταβεβήκει ’had moved on, passed on’)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’) · also dat. of possession with εἰμί: ’who are mine’ (οἵ μοι ἔασιν ’who are mine’)
μυρί: μυρίος — countless, numberless; neut. acc. pl., elided (μυρί’ = μυρία), agreeing with ὀνείατα
μύθῳ: μῦθος — word, speech, plea; masc. dat. sg.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’ · also negating a generic relative clause with the opt.: ὃς μὴ … ἐλάσειε ’whoever did not drive off’
μᾶλλον: μάλα — very, much; comparative adv. μᾶλλον: ’more, rather, the more’
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg. · also a plan, scheme agreed on (τοῖον...τελέωμεν μῦθον ’let us carry out this plan’)
ναιετάων: ναιετάω — dwell, live; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
ναυσίκλυτοι: ναυσικλυτός — famed for ships, ship-renowned; masc. nom. pl.
νηυσὶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. pl., epic νηυσί(ν)
νηός: ναῦς — ship; gen. sg., epic (= Attic νεώς)
νηῒ: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. sg., epic νηΐ (diaeresis marks the two syllables)
νηῦς: ναῦς — ship; nom. sg., epic νηῦς
νοῦσος: νοῦσος — sickness, disease; fem. nom. sg., epic (= Attic νόσος)
ξεῖν: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend; voc. sg., elided (ξεῖν’ = ξεῖνε)
ξεῖνε: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); voc. sg.
ξυνίει: ξυνίημι — perceive, understand, attend to (= συνίημι, ξυν- epic for συν-); pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’attend!’
ξὺν: σύν (epic ξύν) — with, together with; + dat.
οἰχομένοιο: οἴχομαι — be gone, have gone away; pres. part. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), perfect sense: ’gone’
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’) · also encl. dat. sg. of a thing, ’to/for it’ (δύω δέ τέ οἱ θύραι ’and it has two doors’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’those, the’ (οἱ πέπλοι ’the robes’) · also dat. sg. of the giver with δέχομαι: ’from him’ (οἱ ἐδέξατο ’took from him’)
οἴκαδ: οἴκαδε (elided οἴκαδ’) — homeward, to home; adv., -δε suffix of direction
οἷά: οἷος — of what kind, such as; relative/exclamatory adj., neut. nom./acc. pl., with τε in a comparison: ’just as, like’ · also neut. acc. pl. relative, object of a verb: ’such things as’ (οἷά κ’ ἔχωμεν ’such as we may have’)
οἷς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. dat. pl.: ’his own’ (μετὰ οἷς ἑτάροισι ’among his own companions’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: which; masc./neut. dat. pl. (οἷς ἔπι ’on which’, of the stones)
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὕνεκά: οὕνεκα — because, for the reason that (= οὗ ἕνεκα, contracted); conj.
οὗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. gen. sg.: ’whose’ (= Attic οὗ) · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐξ οὗ ’since, from the time when’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own; masc. gen. sg. agreeing with a noun (οὗ πατρὸς ’her own father’s’)
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg.: ’all’ (πάντα δῆμον ’all the people’) · also neut. acc. pl. adverbial: ’altogether, in every respect’ (οὐκ ἄρα πάντα νοήμονες ’not altogether sensible’)
πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
παιδὸς: παῖς — child, daughter; fem. gen. sg. (φίλης ... παιδός ’a dear daughter’) · also masc. gen. sg., ’son’ (παιδὸς ἐμοῖο ’my son’; τοῦ παιδὸς ἀγαυοῦ ’the noble son’)
παρ: παρά (elided παρ’) — beside, among; + dat. · also + gen., ’from, from the side of’ (παρ’ Ἴλου ’from Ilus’) · also + acc., of motion, ’past, along, beside’ (παρ’ Μίμαντα ’past Mimas’)
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’) · also + acc., ’beside, contrary to’ (παρὰ μοῖραν ’beside what is fitting’)
πατρίδος: πατρίς — fatherland, native land; gen. sg.
παῖδα: παῖς — child, son, daughter; masc./fem. acc. sg.
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
πολλὸν: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, epic (= Attic πολύ): ’much’ · also attributive, neut. nom. sg. agreeing with μέθυ: ’much (wine)’ · also neut. acc. sg. as substantive object: ’much (wine)’ · also adj.: ’big’ · also epic πολλόν (= πολύν), masc. acc. sg., agreeing with χρόνον: ’long (time)’
πολύμητις: πολύμητις — of many wiles, epithet of Odysseus (built on μῆτις ’cunning intelligence’); masc. nom. sg.
πολὺς: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. sg., grave accent, mid-clause form (χειμὼν πολὺς ’much winter storm’)
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, formerly; enclitic adv.
ποτὶ: πρός — to, toward, against; prep., epic ποτί, here as preverb in tmesis (ποτὶ … βάλε = προσέβαλε) · also a plain preposition + acc., no tmesis: ποτὶ τοῖχον ’against the wall’ · also + dat. ‘against’ · also + dat., ’on, upon’: ποτὶ χθονί ’on the ground’
προσέειπε: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέειπεν: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf. · also + aor. subj., ’before’ (πρὶν … ἐπέλθῃ ’before it comes upon’) · also + opt.: ’before’ (πρὶν τλαίη ’before he would bring himself’) · also adv. with a finite verb, ’before that, sooner’ (πρὶν … ἀγείρετο ’before that … came gathering’) · also + fut. indic.: ’before’ (πρὶν … γαῖα καθέξει ’before the earth covers’)
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’
πρῶτα: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’first’
πυθέσθαι: πυνθάνομαι — inquire, learn, hear of; aor. inf. mid. πυθέσθαι, epexegetic: ’to hear of’ (κλέος ... πυθέσθαι ’fame ... to hear of’) · also aor. inf. mid., of purpose after a verb of sending: ’to inquire’ (προέμεν πυθέσθαι ’to send forth to inquire’)
πόλλ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl., elided (πόλλ’ = πολλά): ’many’ · also used adverbially: ‘much, often’ (πόλλ’ ἐπέεσσιν ‘again and again with words’)
πόποι: πόποι — (in ὢ πόποι) exclamation of surprise or displeasure: ’ah! well!’; origin unknown
πότνια: πότνια — lady, mistress (title of respect for a goddess); fem. nom. sg. · also of a mortal woman, a respectful title: ’revered, honoured’ (πότνια μήτηρ ’the honoured mother’)
πῖνέ: πίνω — drink; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔπινε); accented πῖνέ before the enclitic τε
σέ: σύ — you (sg.); acc. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’you’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’)
σιγῇ: σιγή — silence; fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ’in silence’
συβῶτα: συβώτης — swineherd; masc. voc. sg., epic -α (in apposition to Εὔμαιε)
σφισι: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. dat. pl. pron. (= Attic αὐτοῖς): ’to/for them’
σῆς: σός — your, yours (sg.); possessive adj., fem. gen. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.; also relative: ’which’ (accented τά before a following enclitic)
τέκε: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., no augment (= ἔτεκε)
τέρπεο: τέρπω — delight, gladden; mid. enjoy oneself; pres. imper. 2 sg. mid., epic uncontracted (= Attic τέρπου)
τέρπεται: τέρπω — delight; mid. take one’s pleasure, enjoy; pres. 3 sg. mid.
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj. · also plain interrogative, direct object/predicate: ’what’ (τί πάθω ’what am I to suffer’; τί ... γένηται ’what is to become’) · also the enclitic indefinite as an adjective agreeing with a noun, accented before enclitic που: εἴ τί που εἴλυμα ’if any wrapper’ · also enclitic indefinite with a negative, ’anything’, as accusative subject of an infinitive (οὐ … τί φημι κακώτερον ἄλλο … συγχεῦαι ’I say nothing else is worse’) · also enclitic indefinite, adverbial without a negative: ’somehow, in some way’ (τοῦτό τί μοι κάλλιστον ’this seems to me somehow the fairest’) · also enclitic indefinite as an adjective after μή, accented before an enclitic: ’any’ (μή τί τοι … πῆμα ’any harm to you’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ὅπως, accented before enclitic μοι: ’any’ (τί … ἄλγος ’any pain’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ἤ, accented before the enclitic μοι: ’any’ (ἤ τί μοι … κειμήλιον ’or any treasure of mine’)
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc. nom. sg. · also the enclitic indefinite τις accented before a following enclitic, not interrogative: ’someone, anyone’ (ἤν τίς τοι εἴπῃσι ’if someone tells you’)
ταῦτά: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’, accented before an enclitic
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τελεύτησάν: τελευτάω — bring to an end, complete; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= Attic ἐτελεύτησαν): ’they completed’
τερπώμεθα: τέρπομαι — take pleasure, enjoy oneself; pres. subj. 1 pl., hortatory
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’) · also ὅ τι as an adverbial acc. in an indirect question: ’why’ · also as a substantive object in a statement: ’something’ (καί τι ἴσασι ’they know something’)
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also with a negative: ’any, anyone’ (οὐ … τις ’no one’; οὐδέ τις ’nor any’) · also after the relative ὅς, indefinite: ὅς τις ’whichever, whoever’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιγὰρ: τοιγάρ — well then, accordingly; particle introducing a response to a request
τοκήων: τοκεύς — parent, begetter; masc. gen. pl.
τούτων: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this, that; gen. pl.: ’of these’
τοῖον: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’in such a way’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun or pronoun: ’such a one as’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’) · also ’so’, qualifying an adj. · also neut. nom./acc. sg., agreeing with a neut. noun: τοῖον … ἔρνος (acc.), τοῖον … δόρυ (nom.) ’such a shoot, such a trunk’
τοῖς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: masc./neut. dat. pl. ’in which, with which’ (τετυγμένα, τοῖς ἐνάμελγεν ’well-made, in which he milked’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. dat. pl.: ’the’ (ἰχθύσι τοῖς ὀλίγοισι ’for the little fishes’)
τοῦδ: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. gen. sg., elided (τοῦδ’ = τοῦδε)
τοῦτ: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. acc. sg., elided (τοῦτ’ = τοῦτο)
τοῦτο: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. sg.
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τόν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg.: ’him’; also relative: ’whom’ · also demonstrative with a noun, ’that’, antecedent of a relative: ἄνδρα τόν, ὅς κε … ’that man who …’
τόσον: τόσος — so much, so great; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially
τόφρα: τόφρα — so long, meanwhile; adv., correlative with ἕως ’until’
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom; fem. acc. sg. (τὴν Ὠκεανὸς τέκε ’whom Oceanus begot’) · also ’the other’, contrasted with a preceding τὴν … μέν: fem. acc. sg. (τὴν δέ ’the other one’) · also article-like with a numeral: ’the one’ (τὴν μὲν ἴαν ’the one portion’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun · also relative adv., ’where, in the place where’ (τῇ δή μοι ἐείσατο χῶρος ἄριστος) · also adverbial, ’in that (event)’, pointing back to a contest just named: τῇ δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύαλος ἀπεκαίνυτο ’in that Euryalus in turn outdid all’ · also relative adv. of manner, with περ: ’in just the way that’ · also adv. of direction, ’thither, that way’ · also with a noun, article-like: fem. dat. sg. ’the’ (τῇ δεκάτῃ ’on the tenth’)
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’ · also with a noun, article-like: τῶν ἄλλων ἀνέμων ’of the other winds’ · also distributive, ’of the one … of the other’ (τῶν μὲν … τῶν δ’ ’of the one band … of the other’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: gen. pl. ’of whom, whose’ (τῶν ὕβρις τε βίη τε … ἵκει ’whose insolence and violence reach’)
φάσθαι: φημί — say, speak; pres. inf. mid., epic φάσθαι (= Attic φάναι)
φέρεσθαι: φέρω — carry; mid. pres. inf.: ’to carry off for oneself’ · also pass. inf., ’to be carried’ (by the wind): Βορέῃ προβάλεσκε φέρεσθαι ’would toss it to the North Wind to be carried’
φίλα: φίλος — dear, one’s own; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially with φρονέω: ’with friendly thoughts, kindly’ · also plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun: ’dear’ (τέκνα φίλα ’dear children’)
φίλει: φιλέω — love, treat as a friend, entertain; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐφίλει)
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: φίλον υἱόν ’dear son’ · also masc. acc. sg. predicative, agreeing with a pronoun: ’as a friend, welcome’ (φίλον ἐλθεῖν)
φίλος: φίλος — dear, dear one; masc. nom. sg. used as voc.: ’friend’ · also plain attributive adjective, not vocative: ’dear’ (φίλος υἱός ’dear son’) · also predicate adjective: ’dear’ (φίλος ἦεν Ἰήσων ’Jason was dear (to her)’)
φαγέμεν: ἐσθίω — eat; aor. φαγεῖν; inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic φαγεῖν): ’to eat’
φαινομένηφι: φαίνω — show; mid. appear; pres. part. mid. fem. dat. sg. with epic -ηφι (= Attic -ῃ): ’appearing’
φθίσθαι: φθίνω — perish, waste away; aor. inf. mid.: ’to have perished’
φιλότητι: φιλότης — friendship, love, affection; fem. dat. sg.
φρένας: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. acc. pl.
φρεσὶ: φρήν — mind, heart, wits; fem. dat. pl.
φῦλ: φῦλον — tribe, race, class; neut. acc. pl., elided (φῦλ’ = φῦλα): ‘tribes’
χ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); elided and aspirated χ’ before a rough breathing
χατέουσιν: χατέω — need, want, desire; pres. part. masc. dat. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic χατοῦσιν); ’for them wanting (to take)’
χλαῖνάν: χλαῖνα — a thick woollen cloak; fem. acc. sg.
χρή: χρή — there is need (of); impersonal verb, + acc. of person and gen. of thing
ἀγανοῖς: ἀγανός — gentle, mild; adj., neut. dat. pl., agreeing with βελέεσσιν
ἀγγελίη: ἀγγελίη — news, message; fem. nom. sg., Ionic η
ἀγλαὰ: ἀγλαός — splendid, shining, glorious; adj., neut. acc. pl. (ἀγλαὰ δῶρα ’splendid gifts’)
ἀγορεύσω: ἀγορεύω — speak out, declare; fut. 1 sg.
ἀγρόθεν: ἀγρόθεν — from the field, from the country; adv. (ἀγρός ’field’ + -θεν)
ἀθανάτοισιν: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. dat. pl., epic (= Attic -οις)
ἀκούειν: ἀκούω — hear, listen to; pres. inf.
ἀλλήλων: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., gen. pl.
ἀλλοθρόους: ἀλλόθροος — of foreign speech, speaking another tongue (ἄλλος + θρόος); masc. acc. pl.
ἀλόχοιο: ἄλοχος — wife, bedfellow; fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἀμείβετο: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented
ἀμφιέσασα: ἀμφιέννυμι — put clothes around, clothe; aor. part. fem. nom. sg.: ’having clothed’
ἀμφοτέρῃσι: ἀμφότερος — both (of two); adj., fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι(ν) (= Attic -αις)
ἀνείρεαι: ἀνείρομαι — ask, inquire; pres. 2 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic -ῃ)
ἀνθρώπους: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; acc. pl.
ἀνθρώπων: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; gen. pl.
ἀντία: ἀντίος — opposite, against; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially, + gen.
ἀνώγει: ἄνωγα (defective, perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; impf. 3 sg., + inf.: ’was bidding’ · also pres. 3 sg., a present formed on the perf. stem: ’bids’ (ἐποτρύνει καὶ ἀνώγει ’urges and bids’)
ἀπέφθιτο: ἀποφθίνω — perish, die; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’had perished’
ἀπήμονά: ἀπήμων — without harm (ἀ- + πῆμα): harmless, doing no harm, or unharmed, safe; masc./fem. acc. sg.
ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀπεπλάγχθης: ἀποπλάζω — drive off course; aor. pass. 2 sg.: ’you were driven astray’
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἀργαλέῳ: ἀργαλέος — hard, grievous, painful; masc. dat. sg.
ἀργυρότοξος: ἀργυρότοξος — of the silver bow; masc. nom. sg., epithet of Apollo
ἀτιτάλλω: ἀτιτάλλω — nurture, raise, tend; pres. 1 sg.
ἀτρεκέως: ἀτρεκής — exact, unswerving; adv. ἀτρεκέως: ’exactly, precisely’
ἀφνειοῖο: ἀφνειός — rich, wealthy; masc. gen. sg., epic -οῖο (= Attic -οῦ)
ἂρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, grave form ἂρ (ἐπεὶ ἂρ δή ’since, as it seems’)
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg. · also ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγε): ’led’ · also ἄγω — lead; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead’ (μή μ’ ἄγε κεῖσ’ ’do not lead me there’)
ἄγοντες: ἄγω — lead, bring; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’bringing, leading’
ἄλγεσι: ἄλγος — pain, grief; neut. dat. pl.
ἄλλ: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. acc. sg., elided (ἄλλ’ = ἄλλο): ’another thing’ · also neut. nom./acc. pl. ἄλλα, elided, genuinely ambiguous with the sg. reading: ἄλλ’ ἐνόησεν ’devised other things’ or ’another thing’ · also the conjunction ἀλλά ’but’, elided, as printed before ἄγε: ἄλλ’ ἄγε δή ’but come now’
ἄλλη: ἄλλος — other, another; fem. nom. sg., adverbial in the idiom ἄλλυδις ἄλλη ’one this way, another that’ · also plain adj., fem. nom. sg.: ’other’ (οὔ τις ... ἄλλη ’no other woman’)
ἄμφω: ἄμφω — both; dual pron./adj., used with a dual verb · also with a plural noun: ἄμφω χεῖρας ’both hands’
ἄξιον: ἄξιος — worth, worthy; neut. nom. sg., + gen.: ’worth (a return)’
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄχεϊ: ἄχος — grief, distress; neut. dat. sg., epic ἄχεϊ (= Attic ἄχει)
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows) · also accented ἐγώ before the enclitic μιν that follows
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκέλευεν: κελεύω — bid, order, urge; impf. 3 sg., movable ν (= Attic ἐκέλευε(ν))
ἐκπάγλως: ἔκπαγλος — terrible, vehement; adv. ἐκπάγλως: ’terribly, vehemently’
ἐλθὼν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having come’
ἐμοί: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg., accented (non-enclitic emphatic): ’to me’
ἐμοῖο: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ἐμὸς: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. nom. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνθάδε: ἐνθάδε — here, to this place; adv., with -δε suffix of direction (’in this place’)
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐπέεσσιν: ἔπος — word; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι(ν)
ἐπέφραδεν: φράζω — point out, show, tell; reduplicated aor. 3 sg. ἐπέφραδε with ν-movable: ’pointed out’
ἐπιμίμνω: ἐπιμίμνω — stay at, persist in; pres. 1 sg., epic (= ἐπιμένω), + dat.
ἐποιχόμενος: ἐποίχομαι — go against, assail, come upon; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ‘assailing’
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’ · also + acc. of time: ’for, over’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + dat., ’in charge of, over’ (ἐπὶ κτεάτεσσιν ’over my possessions’)
ἐρέω: ἐρέω — say, tell, declare; fut. 1 sg. (epic fut. of εἶπον, = Attic ἐρῶ); in tmesis with ἐκ, ἐξερέω ’speak out plainly’
ἐρχομένην: ἔρχομαι — go, come; pres. part. mid. fem. acc. sg.: ’going’
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐτίμα: τιμάω — honour; impf. 3 sg., contracted: ’used to honour’
ἐών: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic ἐών (= Attic ὤν), accented ἐών before a pause: ’being’ (τοῖος ἐών ’being such’)
ἑ: ἕ — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. sg. reflexive/personal pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/-ήν/-ό)
ἑτάρων: ἑταῖρος (epic ἕταρος) — companion, comrade; masc. gen. pl. (= Attic ἑταίρων)
ἑῆος: ἐΰς (ἠΰς) — good, noble; masc. gen. sg., epic ἑῆος/ἐῆος (= Attic ἀγαθοῦ)
ἔδωκα: δίδωμι — give; aor. 1 sg., κ-aorist: ’I gave’
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔλθοι: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. opt. 3 sg. (wish): ’may... come’ · also in a conditional protasis: ’if ... should come’ (εἰ καί ποθεν ἄλλοθεν ἔλθοι)
ἔλθῃ: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. subj. 3 sg.: ’may come’
ἔμπεσεν: ἐμπίπτω — fall upon, fall into; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐνέπεσεν)
ἔμπης: ἔμπης — nevertheless, in any case, for all that; adv.
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’) · also doubled, ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’this way and that’
ἔνι: ἐν — in; prep. + dat., postpositive with anastrophe, accent thrown back after its noun (δήμῳ ἔνι = ἐν δήμῳ) · also = ἔνεστι, ἔνεισι (ἔνι with no case): ’there is, there are in it/among them’ (ἄνδρες νηῶν ἔνι τέκτονες ’men, shipwrights, are among them’)
ἔπιόν: πίνω — drink; aor. 3 pl. (accent from the following enclitic θ’)
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔργον: ἔργον — deed, work, task; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (κακὸν … ἔργον τε ἔπος τε μελέτω ’let no evil deed or word be a care’) · also neut. nom. sg., in apposition/predicative, naming a maker: ἔργον Ἡφαίστοιο ’the work of Hephaestus’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a passive verb: ’work’ (τόδε ἔργον ἀέξεται ’this work grows’)
ἔσκε: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, iterative: ’used to be, was’
ἔστι: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg. impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also existential, ‘there is’ (ἔστι δέ τις πέτρη ‘there is a rock’)
ἔστιν: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also plain copula, personal: ’is’ (ἀργύρεος ... ἔστιν ἅπας ’it is entirely silver’) · also with a dat. of the possessor, ’have’ (ἅσσα μοι ἔστιν ’whatever I have’) · also existential, ’there is’ (ἐν … νηὶ … βρῶσίς τε πόσις τε ἔστιν ’in the ship there is food and drink’)
ἔτ: ἔτι — still, yet; adv., elided (ἔτ’ = ἔτι)
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔῃσιν: εἰμί — be; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσιν (= Attic ᾖ): ’he may be, he is’
ἕκαστα: ἕκαστος — each, every; neut. acc. pl. used substantivally: ’each thing, everything’ · also adjectival, with a noun: ’each piece’ (ὅπλα ἕκαστα) · also neut. nom. pl. in apposition: ’each’ (πεντήκοντα δ’ ἕκαστα ’fifty to each’)
ἕλοντο: αἱρέω — take; aor. mid. 3 pl., unaugmented (= εἵλοντο): ’took (for themselves)’
ἠελίοιο: Ἠέλιος — the Sun (god); gen. sg., epic (-οιο = Attic Ἡλίου)
ἠοῖ: ἠώς — dawn; fem. dat. sg. ἠοῖ
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’ · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a pool of water (ἡ δὲ προσέπλαζε ’and it lapped up’) · also fem. nom. sg. ’it’, of a ship (ἡ δ’ ἔθει ’and it ran’) · also fem. nom. sg. with a noun/adj., article-like: ’the other’ (ἡ δ’ ἄλλη ’and the other woman’) · also fem. nom. sg. article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ἡ γὰρ δμώων δίκη ’for the way of servants’)
ἡμῖν: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; dat. pl. ’to us’
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’ · also ’before’ after a verb of anticipating (ἔφθης … ἢ ἐγώ ’you got here before I did’) · also introducing the first alternative of an indirect question: ’whether’ (ἢ ἔτι … ἦέ τις ’whether still … or someone’) · also ’than’ after a verb of preferring: βουλοίμην … ἢ … ἀνάσσειν ’I would rather … than rule’
ἤ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj., accented before an enclitic (ἤ κεν); ἤ … ἦε ’whether … or’ · also ’than’ after a comparative: μεῖζον … ἤ ’greater than’
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤλυθον: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 1 sg., augmented, epic root ἐλυθ- with epenthetic -υ- (= Attic ἦλθον): ’I have come’ · also aor. 3 pl. (the form serves both persons): ’they came’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥβην: Ἥβη — Hebe, goddess of youth, wife of Heracles in heaven; fem. acc. sg.
ἥμενος: ἧμαι — sit; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’sitting’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἰδυῖα: οἶδα — know; perf. part. fem. nom. sg., here ’skilled, wise’
ἰφθίμῃ: Ἰφθίμη — Iphthime, Penelope’s sister, wife of Eumelus; fem. dat. sg. · also ἴφθιμος — mighty, stout; adj., fem. dat. sg. form, qualifying θυγατέρ’ · also ἴφθιμος, fem. dat. sg., agreeing with ἀλόχῳ: ’mighty (wife)’
ἱκόμεθ: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive; aor. mid. 1 pl., unaugmented, elided (ἱκόμεθ’ = ἱκόμεθα): ’we have come’
ἴδῃ: ὁράω (aor. stem ἰδ-) — see; aor. subj. mid. 2 sg., after ὄφρα: ’that you may see’
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδύρεται: ὀδύρομαι — lament, mourn, make complaint; pres. mid. 3 sg.
ὀλίγον: ὀλίγος — small, little, slight; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg. · also article-like with an adjective and a name: ’the’ (ὁ θρασὺς Ὀδυσσεύς ’bold Odysseus’) · also article-like with a noun: ’the’ (ὁ γέρων ’the old man’) · also distributive, masc. nom. sg.: ’the one’ (ὁ μὲν οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἱκάνει ’the one reaches the broad heaven’)
ὁδαίων: ὁδαῖος — of a journey; neut. gen. pl. as a noun: ’goods carried on a voyage’ (sense debated)
ὁμοῦ: ὁμοῦ — together, together with, at the same place; adv.
ὁπλοτάτην: ὁπλότατος — youngest; superl. fem. acc. sg., with κούρην
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄλεθρον: ὄλεθρος — destruction, ruin, death; acc. sg.
ὄμοσάν: ὄμνυμι — swear; aor. 3 pl. act., unaugmented (= Attic ὤμοσαν): ’they had sworn’
ὄρχαμος: ὄρχαμος — chief, leader; masc. nom. sg. (ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν ’chief of men’)
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary-sequence verb: ὄφρα ... ἕλοις/ἵκοιο ’so that you might take/arrive’ · also temporal + indic., ’as long as’ (ὄφρα μὲν … ἦν ’so long as it was’)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅπῃ: ὅπῃ — where, wherever, in whatever way; relative adv.
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’)
ὅτινα: ὅστις — whoever, whichever; epic ὅτινα, masc. acc. sg.: ’whomever’
ὅτις: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; masc. nom. sg., epic (ὅτις = Attic ὅστις)
ὑμετέρων: ὑμέτερος — your (pl.), yours; masc. gen. pl.
ὑμῖν: σύ (pl. ὑμεῖς) — you; dat. pl.: ’to you’
ὑπερφίαλοι: ὑπερφίαλος — overweening, arrogant; masc. nom. pl.
ὕεσσιν: ὗς (σῦς) — swine; masc./fem. dat. pl., epic -εσσιν (= Attic ὑσί)
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. with a finite verb: ’how (dear) he is’ (ὡς ὅδε … φίλος … ἐστίν) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., of manner: ’as’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I shall say’) · also comparative ’like’, standing before its noun (ὡς νυκτερίς ’like a bat’) · also ὡς ὅθ’ (= ὡς ὅτε), ’as when’, comparing with an occasion in the past (ὡς ὅθ’ ὑπὸ Τροίην ’as when beneath Troy’) · also introducing an indirect statement after a verb of saying: ’that, how’ (εἴποιμ’ ὡς … ἔρχομαι ’I might tell how I am coming’)
ὢ: ὤ — oh! ah! (exclamation, as in ὢ πόποι)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὥρη: ὥρα (Ionic ὥρη) — season, the right time, hour; fem. nom. sg. (Ionic η = Attic ᾱ): ’it is time (for)’
ὦνον: ὦνος — price, purchase price; masc. acc. sg.
ᾗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. dat. sg.: ’for which, to which’ (referring back to the ship, νηῦς) · also ’on which’, of a road: τὴν ὁδὸν ᾗ δὴ ’the journey on which’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: ’his own’, fem. dat. sg., agreeing with ἀλόχῳ (ᾗ … ἀλόχῳ ’his own wife’) · also relative adverb of place, ’where, by which way’ (ᾗ οἱ Ἀθήνη πέφραδε ’where Athena had pointed out to him’)
ᾧ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc. dat. sg.: ’his own (son)’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which; masc. dat. sg. (δοίη δ’ ᾧ κ’ ἐθέλοι ’give her to whom he wished’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν, neut. dat. sg. (same form), agreeing with a neut. noun: πεδίοιο ... ᾧ ἔνι ... ’a plain in which is...’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν, neut. dat. sg., agreeing with ἄχεϊ: ’her own (grief)’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, weak enclitic form ῥα, accented ῥά
